title: Mathematical Derivation of Conservative Force as Negative Potential Gradient
assumptions: Smooth spatial coordinates x, y, z
starting_principles: Definition of potential energy differential dU = - dW_c = - (F_x dx + F_y dy + F_z dz)

ordered_steps.explanation: Write total differential of scalar function U(x, y, z) using partial derivatives.
ordered_steps.equation_latex: dU = \frac{\partial U}{\partial x} \, dx + \frac{\partial U}{\partial y} \, dy + \frac{\partial U}{\partial z} \, dz

ordered_steps.explanation: Equate with the physical definition of potential energy differential dU = - (F_x dx + F_y dy + F_z dz).
ordered_steps.equation_latex: -\left( F_x \, dx + F_y \, dy + F_z \, dz \right) = \frac{\partial U}{\partial x} \, dx + \frac{\partial U}{\partial y} \, dy + \frac{\partial U}{\partial z} \, dz

ordered_steps.explanation: Since dx, dy, dz are independent arbitrary displacements, equate corresponding components.
ordered_steps.equation_latex: F_x = -\frac{\partial U}{\partial x}, \quad F_y = -\frac{\partial U}{\partial y}, \quad F_z = -\frac{\partial U}{\partial z} \implies \vec{F} = -\nabla U

limiting_cases: For 1D spring U = 1/2 k x^2, F_x = -d(1/2 k x^2)/dx = -kx (recovering Hooke's law)
For near-surface gravity U = mgy, F_y = -d(mgy)/dy = -mg (recovering downward weight)
claim_traces: HCV1 Ch 8 p. 137; HRW Ch 8 p. 204; UP Ch 7 p. 252
